turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Keane, in you come. The spirometry is done already. Doctor is just fighting with the computer.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry about that, the screen's after freezing on me again. Mr Keane, what brings you in today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor. Thank you for fitting me in. I have a cough each morning, and I become short of breath when I walk out.
[SEG0004] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'm Aoife Dunne, his carer on weekday mornings. He asked me to come in with him.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Grand. How long have you had this morning cough?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): For years, Doctor. Well, it has been a good deal worse these past three weeks.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): The screen jumped on me. Would you repeat that, the timing?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Of course. The cough has been there for years, but it has been worse for about three weeks.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the shortness of breath, is that the same story?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): It has come on gradually. I manage about the house, but the walk to the chemist leaves me quite breathless. Yesterday I had to stop on the hill.
[SEG0011] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He sat on the wall a good two minutes. He makes light of it, Doctor.
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): I am afraid that is accurate.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is there phlegm with it?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): A little in the mornings, mostly clear. When I had the infection it was yellow.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): When was that infection?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): About three weeks ago. A chest infection. I was given amoxicillin, and I finished the course.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): The dose, if you have it?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Five hundred milligrams, three times a day. Well, actually, for five days, not a week. I did finish them.
[SEG0019] person_4 (CAREGIVER): They also gave him steroid tablets. He stopped those.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. Prednisolone, thirty milligrams each morning. I took it for two days only, then I stopped it. It made me very shaky.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so you stopped the prednisolone after two days. Any inhalers at home?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): I have the blue inhaler. I use it when I am wheezy, not on any regular schedule.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this box has popped up. Say that again, the blue inhaler?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Salbutamol, the blue one. Two puffs when I need it. Some days once or twice, and some days not at all.
[SEG0025] person_4 (CAREGIVER): And there's the purple inhaler. He's supposed to use that every day, and he often doesn't.
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): That is correct, I regret to say. The purple inhaler is Seretide. It is meant to be twice a day. I manage it perhaps three or four days in the week.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): The prescription text is tiny on here. What strength is the Seretide?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Um, I believe it is the two hundred and fifty, though I could not be certain.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): I do, Doctor. About ten a day.
[SEG0031] person_4 (CAREGIVER): It's more than ten. I've watched him finish one packet and open another before the evening.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): You are right to correct me. I do minimise it. Well, maybe twenty a day would be nearer the truth.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Say that once more, please. How many cigarettes?
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): About twenty a day. I have smoked since I was seventeen, fifty years, near enough.

[SEG0035] person_1 (NURSE): Will I read the spirometry while you have the chart open? FEV1 was one point six litres, sixty-two percent predicted. FVC two point nine litres. The ratio came out at fifty-five percent.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hang on, this window won't shut. The FEV1 again?
[SEG0037] person_1 (NURSE): One point six litres, sixty-two percent predicted. Ratio fifty-five percent. And his oxygen saturation was ninety-four percent on room air.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): None that I know of, Doctor.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): A water tablet, blood pressure tablets, anything else from the chemist?
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): I was never given a water tablet. I do take an ordinary multivitamin in the morning. Nothing for blood pressure.
[SEG0042] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He wheezes at night as well, especially after a heavier day of smoking.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, there is a night-time wheeze. I should have mentioned it.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever now, chest pain, or blood in the phlegm?
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever now. No chest pain. I have never coughed up blood.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll have a listen. There's a soft wheeze at both bases. No crackles. You're not hot to the touch.
[SEG0047] person_1 (NURSE): Observations from before you came in: pulse eighty-eight, blood pressure one thirty-two over seventy-eight, respiratory rate eighteen, temperature thirty-six point six.

[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Putting it together, this is most likely smoking-related COPD. The spirometry sits with that, though I wouldn't call it fully confirmed today. The chest infection looks to have settled.
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): I understand. What ought I to do?

[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take the purple inhaler properly, twice every day, not three days a week. Keep the blue one for when you are breathless or wheezy. And I would like to refer you to the smoking cessation service, if you are willing.
[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): I would be grateful for that help. I know I ought to stop.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll arrange a chest x-ray as well, with the smoking history and the recent infection.
[SEG0053] person_4 (CAREGIVER): The bus was desperate this morning, but that's neither here nor there. Does he need to be seen again?
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in six weeks so we can check the inhalers are actually happening. Sooner if you are more breathless, or if the phlegm goes yellow again.
[SEG0055] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. I shall follow that. Good day to you.
